# Shared AI client

`@katalon-experiments/ai-client` sends serialized OpenAI Responses directly
to `https://api.openai.com/v1` using `OPENAI_API_KEY`. OpenRouter is used only
for native JEV System One and its TypeSafe endpoint catalog, using
`LOKI_OPENROUTER_API_KEY` or `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`. Keys are independent.

```js
import { providerConnection, sendFetch } from "@katalon-experiments/ai-client";
const connection = providerConnection(
  "https://api.openai.com/v1/responses",
  process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY,
);
const response = await sendFetch(connection, {
  method: "POST",
  body: existingSerializedNativeRequest,
  signal: existingAbortSignal,
});
```

The client preserves serialized bytes, model/reasoning fields, native responses,
usage, errors, streaming and cancellation. It adds no retries, replay, model
selection or success interpretation. `providerConnection` refuses embeddings,
OpenRouter Responses, arbitrary endpoints and credential-bearing URLs.

`LOKI_LITELLM_ENABLED` and `LOKI_LITELLM_ORIGIN` cannot redirect these native
routes. Their historical parsers, convenience client and embeddings route are retained
in `experiments/2173-reasoning-support/provider-transport`; Product exports only
its selected native serialized transport and accounting helpers. The native profile requires provider keys; the separately selected managed Codex host is described below. Fetch redirects are refused;
Node HTTP requests do not follow redirects. Inherited Authorization is replaced
with the credential for the selected native endpoint.

Callers with exact serialization and evidence contracts use
`providerConnection(nativeUrl, key, env)` plus `sendFetch` or `requestHttp`.
Their original bounded readers, deadlines, Stop, partial-byte retention and
unknown-charge rules remain in their own components. `lunaUsageEstimate` derives
standard-tier costs from valid native usage using official Luna rates checked
30 October 2026. The caller must label that value as an estimate rather than a
billing receipt. Missing/invalid usage returns null, never an invented zero.

Consumers bundle this dependency into their immutable package. Run `npm test`
for controlled transport tests; these do not make paid inference calls or prove
live-provider acceptance. Historical archives and experiment entrypoints are
not migrated by this change. Hai's routing decision is recorded in
[#2161](https://github.com/katalon-studio/loki/issues/2161#issuecomment-6517382712).

## Managed Codex host

A host-bound `LOKI_AUTH_BROKER_SOCKET` selects the private Unix channel for the
Codex shared-auth build. This is a public local address, not a provider credential.
The broker owns OAuth and forwards the explicit operation through Core to LiteLLM.
`sendFetch` and `requestHttp` retain serialization, cancellation and streaming;
channel failure never switches to the direct route. Without that host binding,
the native OpenAI/JEV behavior above remains unchanged. Existing legacy LiteLLM
flags still cannot redirect calls. See [the Product contract](../../docs/product-design/codex-shared-auth.md).

### Private retained-conversation binding

Retained Planner callers first use private `GET /ai/connection`. The broker reads
Core connection status using the same broker-owned grant ID it returns. The host
hashes that ID with the local data scope and Core account/workspace identity,
then freezes `LOKI_AI_CONNECTION_BINDING` in the operation environment. The value
is a local fence, not a credential, a model input or a new MCP parameter.

With that environment, `providerConnection` selects `/ai-bound/...` and owns the
`x-kaijan-ai-connection` header. The broker checks it after any refresh, at the
synchronous step that captures the bearer token for the Core request. A new grant
rotates the ID, including reconnecting the same account; normal refresh and
restart preserve it. A changed ID returns terminal HTTP412. Missing bindings and
older brokers refuse; retained producers do not fall back to the unbound route
or generate a replacement plan/assessment. Saved reports remain readable.

Legacy grants with a valid saved telemetry epoch use that existing UUID until
normal refresh persists the dedicated ID. Older grants without either ID receive
a metadata-only update under the auth lifecycle fence. It preserves tokens,
permissions and expiry; logout waits for that write before deleting credentials.
A failed metadata write preserves the original grant and unbound operations.

The fixed bound catalog also prepares native
`/openai_passthrough/v1/responses/input_tokens` for #3868. Count and generation
must carry the same ID; a count under one grant cannot admit generation under a
replacement. This does not enable Product counting, establish provider parity or
select numerical budgets. This transport refuses direct/unbound native count.
The private header is removed before Core and cannot be sent on direct transport.
Other existing callers keep their current route until explicitly integrated.

## Agents SDK transport boundary

The `./agents` export provides `createRetainedAgentRunner({ model, store, dispatch })`.
It creates the SDK execution engine for either Planner or Runner; it does not
add another agent or an MCP tool. The capability supplies its agent definition,
scoped tools and saved-operation state when it calls the engine's `run` method.
This adapter alone does not switch the existing planner or browser loop.

`dispatch(body, { signal })` receives the SDK-converted Responses request. The
capability must save the exact outgoing request, dispatch intent and original
response or failure before returning the parsed response or throwing. It keeps
its current managed/native routing, authentication, response validation,
accounting and uncertain-outcome policy. This callback is the only transport:
there is no API-key fallback, SDK retry or remote trace export. The owner must
supply the storage mode; agent settings cannot silently change it or the model.
Leave the model field on each Agent unset, including handoff targets. The engine
rejects explicit names and custom model objects before they send a request.
Streaming is explicitly unsupported by this initial boundary. After retention,
the adapter admits only a completed, error-free response from the selected model.
Other states stop before SDK tools or another turn: a queued/empty response is
not permission to repeat the request. The capability still owns its deeper
schema and evidence validation.

The pinned SDK modules are `@openai/agents-core` and `@openai/agents-openai` 0.21.0.
Using those modules avoids importing realtime/browser-only types into this Node
package. A one-line package patch corrects the optional `agentToolInvocation`
declaration to admit the `undefined` value already returned by the SDK getter.
It changes no JavaScript and keeps strict `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` and
`skipLibCheck: false` in force. Recheck the need for this patch at an SDK upgrade.

The no-network tests execute a real SDK loop, structured output and a function
tool continuation. They also cover cancellation, continuation IDs, no retry,
no default network or trace, and fixed model/storage settings. They are transport
controls, not acceptance of agent prompt quality or an installed workflow.
